source: NCERT Class XI, Themes in World History, Ch. 4 (The Three Orders).

sections.heading: 1. Feudal Society and the Three Orders
points: The chapter deals with **feudalism in Western Europe** (roughly 9th–16th centuries), especially **France**.
Society was divided into **three orders**: those who **pray (clergy)**, those who **fight (nobility/knights)**, and those who **work (peasants)**.
**Feudalism** = a system of relationships based on **land held in return for service**; the **fief** was granted by a lord to a vassal.

sections.heading: 2. The Nobility and the Church
points: The **nobility (lords and knights)** held land, controlled peasants, and provided military service; the **manor** was the basic economic unit.
Knights were a specialised warrior class; **chivalry** was their code.

The **Catholic Church** was immensely powerful — it held vast land, collected **tithes (a tenth of produce)**, and shaped daily life; the **Pope** was its head; **monasteries** were centres of learning and religion.

sections.heading: 3. The Peasants — Free and Serfs
points: Peasants, the majority, were of two kinds: **free peasants** and **serfs (unfree)**, bound to the lord's land.
Serfs owed **labour services, rents and dues** to the lord and could not leave without permission.
Peasant life was hard; the manorial economy relied on their labour; the **three-field system** improved farming.

sections.heading: 4. Change — Towns, Trade and Decline of Feudalism
points: From the 11th century, **towns and trade revived**; a new **class of merchants and townspeople** emerged.
The **Fourteenth-century crisis** (famine, the **Black Death/plague**, and wars) caused huge population loss and weakened feudal ties.
The **decline of feudalism** followed the rise of centralised monarchies ('feudal monarchies'), money economy, and free labour.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three orders: those who pray (clergy), fight (nobility), and work (peasants).
Feudalism = land (fief) granted by lord to vassal in return for service.
The Church collected tithes (a tenth of produce); Pope = head.
Serfs = unfree peasants bound to the lord's land.
Black Death (14th c. plague) + famine weakened feudalism.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **three orders** = clergy (pray), nobility (fight), peasants (work).
A **fief** was land granted to a **vassal** in return for service.
**Tithe** = one-tenth of produce paid to the **Church**.
The **Black Death** was the 14th-century **plague** that hastened feudalism's decline.
